## Background

Today we are going to learn all about the **ggplot2** package in R.


There are tonnes of graphics packages in R. These include "base R graphics" (like the 'plot()' function we used last class) and add on packages like **ggplot2**.

### Comparing base graphics with ggplot

We can use the in-built dataframe 'cars' to play with plotting:

```{r}
head(cars, 3)
tail(cars, 3)
```

---
**Base R plot:**
```{r}
plot(cars)
```

**Now with ggplot:**
First we need to install the package.
However, we don't wnat to install the package more than once, so either put a "#" in front of the install command ('install.packages("ggplot2")') or run it in the console only.
```{r}
#Installing ggplot (only for the first run):
#install.packages("ggplot2")

#load ggplot2:
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(cars)
```

Every ggplot needs at least 3 thing:

- the **data** (data.frame we want to plot from)
- the **aesthetics** (how the columns of the data map to the plot)
- the **geom** (how you want the plot drawn - points, lines, etc)

```{r}
ggplot(data=cars, aes(x=speed, y=dist)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method=lm, color="skyblue") +
  #geom_line()
  theme_grey() +
  labs(x="Speed (mph)", 
       y="Distance (ft)",
       title = "Silly Plot about Cars")
```

'ggplot()' is easier to customize in the long run than base R 'plot()'.

Important side quest: get ggcats:
```{r}
# install.packages("remotes")
# remotes::install_github("R-CoderDotCom/ggcats@main")
library(ggcats)
grid <- expand.grid(1:5, 3:1)

df <- data.frame(x = grid[, 1],
                 y = grid[, 2],
                 image = c("nyancat", "bongo",
                           "colonel", "grumpy",
                           "hipster", "lil_bub",
                           "maru", "mouth",
                           "pop", "pop_close", 
                           "pusheen", "pusheen_pc",
                           "toast", "venus",
                           "shironeko"))

ggplot(df) +
   geom_cat(aes(x, y, cat = image), size = 5) +
   geom_text(aes(x, y - 0.5, label = image), size = 2.5) +
   xlim(c(0.25, 5.5)) + 
   ylim(c(0.25, 3.5))
```


Now lets make some major improvements to the "cars" plot
```{r}
ggplot(data=cars, aes(x=speed, y=dist)) +
  geom_cat(cat="pop", size=2)
```

## Gene expression plot

Read the dataframe from the URL:
```{r}
url <- "https://bioboot.github.io/bimm143_S20/class-material/up_down_expression.txt"
genes <- read.delim(url)
head(genes)
ggplot(genes, aes(Condition1, Condition2)) +
  geom_point() 
```

Q. How many genes are in this dataset?
```{r}
nrow(genes)
ncol(genes)
colnames(genes)
```

Q. How many genes are upregulated?
```{r}
table(genes$State)
sum(genes$State == "up")
#calculate the percentage of genes that are upregulated
sum(genes$State == "up")/nrow(genes)*100
```

Q. What percentage of genes are downregulated?
```{r}
sum(genes$State == "down")/nrow(genes)*100
#rounding
round(sum(genes$State == "down")/nrow(genes)*100, 2)
```


Color datapoints based on "State"
```{r}
p <- ggplot(genes, aes(Condition1, Condition2, color=State)) +
  geom_point()
p
```

```{r}
p_color <- p + 
  scale_color_manual(values = c("skyblue","grey","orange"))
p_labeled <- p_color +
  labs(x = "Control (no drug)",
       y = "Drug treated",
       title = "Gene expression changes upon drug treatment",
       subtitle = "GLP-1 inhibitor from Novo")
p_labeled
```

Making figure panels
```{r}
#install.packages("patchwork")
library("patchwork")
# Setup some example plots 
p1 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_point(aes(mpg, disp))
p2 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_boxplot(aes(gear, disp, group = gear))
p3 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_smooth(aes(disp, qsec))
p4 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_bar(aes(carb))

# Use patchwork to combine them here:
(p1 | p2) /
(p3 | p4)

p_labeled +
  facet_wrap(~State)
```


Trying to plot "up", "down", "unchanging" as different cats
```{r, eval=FALSE}
#modify the dataframe to have "cats" column
genes$cat <- factor(genes$State, labels = c("grumpy", "mouth", "pop"))
#now we plot
p_cat <- ggplot(genes, aes(Condition1, Condition2)) +
  geom_cat(aes(cat = cat), size=1)
p_cat
#HAPPY DAY!
```

## The GapMinder data

The gapminder dataset is famous but sad.
```{r}
# File location online
url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jennybc/gapminder/master/inst/extdata/gapminder.tsv"

gapminder <- read.delim(url)
# install.packages("dplyr")  ## un-comment to install if needed
library(dplyr)

```

Q. How many data entries are there?
```{r}
head(gapminder)
nrow(gapminder)
```


Q. How many countries are in this dataset?
```{r}
head(gapminder$country)
length(unique(gapminder$country))
```

```{r}
ggplot(gapminder, aes(log(gdpPercap), lifeExp, col = continent)) +
  geom_point(aes(alpha=year)) +
  facet_wrap(~continent)

#histogram
ggplot(gapminder) +
  aes(lifeExp, fill = continent) +
  geom_histogram()

#boxplot
ggplot(gapminder) +
  aes(x=lifeExp, continent, fill=continent) +
  geom_boxplot()
```
